report.title: First calibration
report.summary: Six fictional roles that demonstrate direct, adjacent, and boundary-case evidence without using a real candidate's information.

jobs.title: Product Software Engineer
jobs.recommendation: Strong product-engineering alignment with direct evidence for end-to-end TypeScript delivery, customer-facing ownership, and relational data work.

requirements.requirement: Own customer-facing features end to end
requirements.evidence: The fictional candidate led discovery, implementation, deployment, and maintenance for production web products.
Multiple production services and applications used TypeScript and Node.js.
Designed PostgreSQL schemas and data-backed product workflows.

risks: The posting does not state how often the Chicago team meets in person.

companyPolicy.summary: The fictional employer asks candidates to keep no more than three active applications at once.

jobs.title: Full-Stack Engineer
jobs.recommendation: Direct fit for a balanced product role involving APIs, workflow automation, authentication, and regulated customer data.

requirements.evidence: Delivered authenticated applications with role-based access and privacy-sensitive workflows.
Owned REST APIs and third-party integrations in production.
Built privacy-sensitive scheduling software, but not in this employer's clinical specialty.

gaps: No direct experience with the employer's clinical specialty.

jobs.title: Backend Product Engineer
jobs.recommendation: Strong backend and data alignment; the main calibration question is whether weekly New York attendance is acceptable.

requirements.evidence: Owned Node.js APIs from architecture through production maintenance.
Improved production queries and designed indexed relational schemas.
Implemented billing, payment-provider integrations, and transaction history.

risks: The role requires weekly attendance in New York.

jobs.title: Software Engineer, Internal Tools
jobs.recommendation: Most daily product and workflow work is supported, with an adjacent gap around the employer's Python-heavy automation layer.

requirements.evidence: Created internal review, moderation, and publishing tools used in daily operations.
Translated editorial and operations requirements into maintained software.
Used Python for data processing, but the primary production stack was TypeScript.

gaps: Python is central to part of the automation layer.
risks: The exact split between application work and platform maintenance is unclear.

jobs.title: Growth Engineer
jobs.recommendation: The technical and product work transfers, but this is intentionally included to calibrate on-site relocation and experimentation-heavy scope.

requirements.evidence: Owned onboarding and paid-product workflows, but not a dedicated experimentation program.
Built production TypeScript applications across client and server boundaries.
Relocation preference has not been confirmed.

gaps: No dedicated growth-experimentation ownership is documented.
risks: Requires relocation and full-time on-site work.

jobs.title: Staff Platform Engineer
jobs.recommendation: Boundary case for calibration only: general production ownership transfers, but staff-level platform scope is not directly established.

requirements.evidence: The fictional evidence shows product architecture, not organization-wide platform leadership.
Deployed containerized services but did not own a Kubernetes platform.
Maintained and debugged production services with performance and reliability responsibility.

gaps: Staff platform leadership is not supported.
risks: The role's identity is infrastructure rather than product engineering.
